thread:
alice.nguyen: Hey team, incoming escalation from AcmeApp — they see streaming responses cut off ~25-35s into the stream. Client reconnects, but final chunk is missing (they get truncated JSON). They say it used to be fine last week. Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/ACME-4521 :grimacing:

javier.sre: Can you paste the proxy/nginx/alb logs and the raw SSE body (if available)? Also which client (lang/version) and region?

priya.clienteng: Repro info from customer:
- region: us-west-2
- client: acme-js-sdk v2.1.3 (browser)
- steps: open streaming chat, it emits several tokens, then silence, then reconnect. After reconnect they GET /events with Last-Event-ID and get only newer events, but the response never contains the final "assistant":"DONE" object we expect.

alice.nguyen: Pasting the small excerpt they collected (redacted):
```
-- client SSE stream --
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
id: 12345
retry: 3000
data: {"type":"token","text":"Hello, here's a lo"
data: {"type":"token","text":"t of conte"
data: {"type":"token","text":"nt that ends mid-"
\n// then silence for ~28s, connection closes
```

alice.nguyen: Proxy log (ALB) at the moment of drop: `upstream_response_timeout` and then `target terminated connection` entries.

javier.sre: Looks like two possible classes: 1) edge/ALB idle or upstream timeout closing connection mid-response, 2) client-level TCP reset on flaky mobile network. Need packet-level proof. Can you ask customer to run this repro with --no-buffer and capture a tcpdump if possible? Also get our runtime logs around request id 12345.

priya.clienteng: I also asked for user agent and reported network: iPhone Safari 16, behind corporate proxy. I suspect the corporate proxy performs deep idle timeouts and drops keepalives. Their browser may not be sending comment pings.

alice.nguyen: Customer reports they were seeing comment pings in older SDK but upgraded and now rely on TCP keepalive only. They said "we thought TCP keepalive covered it".

javier.sre: Important differentiate: TCP keepalive is kernel-level and on many mobile/corp NATs it's not enough. Our recommended approach for SSE is lightweight comment pings (e.g., `:

` every 15s) or explicit `:ping` events. Do we currently emit comment pings from the edge?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Deployment redwood/edge-streaming v2026.02 rolled at 1765432000 (hash: ab12cd).

alice.nguyen: @javier I pulled the edge config — current idle ping interval is disabled by default for Hosted. We do have an opt-in header `X-Redwood-Stream-Ping: comment|event` per-connection but customers often don't set it.

javier.sre: Action plan:
1) Request tcpdump + curl --no-buffer repro from customer with Last-Event-ID behavior. Provide snippet: `curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/xxx"`
2) Check our runtime logs around request id 12345 for `upstream closed` vs `client aborted` vs `write failed` errors.
3) Short-term mitigation: enable server-side comment pings for this customer's pool via header rewrite at edge (we can inject `: 

` every 15s). Priya, can you ask for permission to toggle?
4) Long-term: consider opt-out for comment pings for Hosted to improve reliability for flaky networks; need to evaluate cost/idle connections.

priya.clienteng: I sent the tcpdump/curl instructions and a quick consent form for toggling pings. Also shared a suggested client patch (acme-js-sdk) to add `:ping

` every 12s as fallback.

alice.nguyen: Customer returned a tiny tcpdump showing TCP FIN from client after ~29s, followed by ALB closing the connection. They also have corporate proxy logs showing 30s idle timeout.

javier.sre: That nails it — proxy kills idle connections at 30s. If our stream goes silent longer than 30s (e.g., long generation pauses, or backpressure), the proxy tears the connection. So two fixes: 1) server-side comment pings to keep flow; 2) recommend client-side frequent flushes or pings.

priya.clienteng: Repro curl command I asked them to run (works for debugging):
```
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream?model=redwood-alpha"
```
and with `--no-buffer` to avoid libcurl buffering.

alice.nguyen: I toggled the header injection for AcmeApp pool to `X-Redwood-Stream-Ping: comment` on their tenant (edge rule) — will monitor.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Edge rule change applied at 1765432200 for tenant acmeapp.

priya.clienteng: Customer confirmed after toggle they received the final chunk on the next run. They said: "looks fixed for now, thanks!" :tada:

javier.sre: Follow-ups:
- Engineering: consider default server-side comment pings in Hosted (configurable). File a small RFC and include perf impact estimate.
- DevEx: update SDK quickstart + examples to show how to enable client pings and use curl reproduction steps.
- Support: mark ticket ACME-4521 as workaround applied; keep monitoring 48h.

alice.nguyen: I'll add logs and timeline to the ticket and keep the support thread open until 48h elapsed.

support-bot: support-bot: Ticket ACME-4521 updated with root cause: corporate proxy idle timeout; mitigation: server-injected comment pings.

alice.nguyen: Thanks all. If anyone wants the raw captures I can paste them in the ticket (redacted).

javier.sre: Nice triage. For the RFC: include option to emit either comment pings or lightweight event `event:ping
data: {}`

priya.clienteng: Noted. Closing this thread after we confirm 48h OK.

alice.nguyen: Closing notes: customer suggested we document difference between TCP keepalive vs SSE comment pings in troubleshooting KB. Added to backlog. :memo:
